No.10583/2025, which is an application seeking grant of leave to appeal under Section 378(4) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 is filed being aggrieved of judgment dated 20.12.2024 passed by learned 3rd Additional Sessions Jude, Umariya, District Umariya in ST No.33/2022 whereby learned trial Court has acquitted all the three accused persons from charges under Sections 376, 376(2)(n), 376(d), 120-B, 342, 506, 376(2)(j), 328, 109 of IPC and under Section 67 of Information Technology (Amended) Act in the matter of State of M.P. sentences.text: 2. Learned counsel for the appellant - victim submits that this appeal is filed under Section 41 of the Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 against the said judgment of acquittal.

3. It is submitted that prosecution story, in short, is that on 11.11.2021, NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:55490 2 CRA-4495-2025 prosecutrix had submitted a written complaint to the effect that she was married to accused No.2 Varun Dhakad, seven years ago in the year 2014 with the consent of the family.
Her husband accused Varun Dhakad was working at a Maruti Suzuki showroom at Jabalpur till January, 2020 after which Varun lost his private job, due to which he was staying at home.

4. Sister-in-law of the victim i.e. accused No.3 works in the Railway Department at Jabalpur, who came to stay at her matrimonial home for a few days in the year 2020 when accused Lakshya Keshwani, who works in her office, often visited her house to meet her sister-in-law when she also got acquainted with Lakshya Keshwani.
5. On 5.01.2021, her husband i.e. accused No.2 Varun Dhakad and co- accused Lakshya had made a plan to visit Bandhavgarh.

On 06.02.2021, as per programme, they were required to go to Bandhavgarh that is she along with her husband and Lakshya Keshwani were required to go to Bandhavgarh but when Lakshya Keshwani came to her house at 4:00 pm on his motorcycle, then Varun refused himself on the pretext of some urgent work and asked her to proceed with Lakshya with an assurance to follow her.

6. Allegation is that Lakshya took her to a prebooked room at Wild Tiger Resort and and there some alcoholic beverage was offered which when was recused by the victim, then she was given some cold drink laced with some sedative, as a result of which she lost her consciousness and when on the next morning she gained her consciousness, she found herself to be physically exploited.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:55490 3 CRA-4495-2025 7.

It is, thus, submitted that there being plethora of evidence available on record to substantiate her case, and that was appropriately produced by the victim yet learned trial Court has wrongly rejected her contentions and acquitted the accused persons, therefore, this appeal under Section 413 of BNSS.

8. Learned Public Prosecutor for the State Shri Ajay Tamrakar supports impugned judgment and submits that its a case of proper appreciation of evidence and even State has, therefore, not filed any appeal.
9. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record.
FIR (Ex.P-2) was lodged on 11.11.2021 showing that incident took place between 06.02.2021 to 08.02.2021.
Only two accused persons have been named, namely, Lakshya Keshwani and Varun Dhakad in the FIR.
10. Under the column dealing with reasons for delay in reporting by the complainant/informant, it is mentioned that because of fear and shame she could not lodge report at earlier point of time.
11. Allegation is that Lakshya kept her in the room of the lodge for two days and violated her privacy on several occasions.
It is further alleged that Varun Dhakad after obtaining money from Lakshya Keshwani had sent her to Bandhavgarh with a view to facilitate Lakshya to violate her privacy.

12. Statements of the victim recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. on 22.11.2021 is available on record as Ex.P-5.

2 13.
Vide Ex.P-6, two photographs of the victim and Lakshya were seized on being produced by the victim.

14. Ex.P-7 is the certificate issued by the victim under Section 65-B of the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:55490 4 CRA-4495-2025 Indian Evidence Act to the effect that she had taken out her photographs with Lakshya Keshwani from her android mobile Redmi 10 Pro and had taken out printouts of those photographs from her laptop and printer.

sentences.text: During the whole period of the said transaction, her mobile, laptop and printer were properly functioning and there has been no editing in the said photographs.

15. Ex.P-8 is the MLC report of the victim in which it is mentioned that she had suffered some head injury and was having small contusion on right temporal bone with oedema and fracture of left clavicle.
This prescription issued by Jabalpur Hospital and Research Centre though bear signatures of one Dr. Alok Agrawal, Neurosurgeon but no date is mentioned on this certificate.
16. Ex.P-9 is the discharge summary of the victim issued by the All India Institute of Medical Sciences, Bhopal, showing her date of admission on 11.02.2021 and date of discharge on 24.02.2021.

entities.text: All India Institute of Medical Sciences, Bhopal
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Her admission was made in the Department of Orthopedics but it is mentioned that she was diagnosed to suffer from SDH right parietal lobe with left parietal lobe contusion, fracture of left parietal bone to left occipital bone, fracture of left clavicle and neck of left scapula (floating shoulder).

In the history, it is mentioned that victim was admitted with a history of road transport accident on 08.02.2021 at 9:00 pm following which she sustained head injury and developed pain,
swelling and restriction of movement in the left shoulder.

17. When this fact is examined in the light of her written complaint dated 11.11.2021 (Ex.P-1) and the FIR (Ex.P-2), then it is evident that she had sustained road transport accident on 08.02.2021, as is mentioned in the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:55490 5 CRA-4495-2025 discharge summary of All India Institute of Medical Sciences, Bhopal.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 18. She was admittedly discharge on 24.02.2021, therefore, delay from 24.02.2021 till 11.11.2021 even if period of COVID is discounted from later part of March, 2021 to June, 2021 is not explained by the victim.
19. Vide Ex.P-10, her mobile, pubic hair and underwear were seized at CHC, Manpur.
20. Vide Ex.P-11 semen slide of accused Lakshya Keshwani along with his pubic hair and underwear were seized at CHC, Manpur.

21. Ex.P-12 is the statement of sister-in-law of the victim under section 161 of Cr.P.C. which was recorded on 21.01.2022 and proved by PW-3.
22.
Vide Ex.P-15, one Bajaj motorcycle was seized from Lakshya Keshwani.
Samples were sent for FSL examination.

Vide Ex.

P-19, visitor's register of Wild Tiger Resort was seized to prove that victim and Lakshya had stayed in that Resort in room No.301 from 06.02.2021 and had produced their Aadhar Card as an I.D.
24.
Ex.P-20 is the Medical Examination Report of Lakshya Keshwani wherein Dr. Abhishek Mishra (PW-11) has stated that he was able to perform masturbation and sexual intercourse with full efficiency.
25. Ex.P-21 is the MLC of the victim carried out by Dr. Abhishek Mishra (PW-11).

In the history is mentioned that as per her statement she was in friendship with the accused since 10 months and physical relationship with accused, her BP pulse were normal, her secondary sexual characters were well developed, opinion was that no exact opinion can be given regarding recent sexual intercourse as there are no signs and symptoms of recent NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:55490 6 CRA-4495-2025 intercourse but has been sexually active previously.
For more confirmations all the collected items are sealed, preserved and handed over to police constable.
26. Ex.P-22 is the Seizure Memo of mobile of Lakshya Keshwani.
27. Ex.P-28 is the Hotel Passenger Register.
28. Ex.P-37 is the copy of Arrest Memo, by which Varun Dhakad was arrested on 26.05.2022.
29. Ex.P-39 is the Arrest Memo of Vineeta Dhakad, by which she was arrested on 26.05.2022.

30. Ex.P-41 is the Forensic Report from the State Forensic Science Laboratory, Sagar, in which it is mentioned that on item A - Vaginal Slide, item B - Pubic Hair, item C - Panty of the victim and item E of the accused, no human sperms were found, then there are two photographs as Article A & B showing intimate photographs of the victim with the appellant Lakshya.

31. Victim (PW-1) after having narrated the incident, as mentioned in the FIR, in para 7, admits that she had asked the accused Lakshya on 08.02.2021 to take her to Jabalpur and she will not say anything to anybody.
32. In para 8, she stated that she had consumed a cup of tea which was laced with sedatives and thereafter she had become unconscious.
She gained consciousness after fifteen days.
For sometime she was admitted at Jabalpur Hospital and, therefore, her parents had taken her to the AIIMS Hospital, Bhopal as her husband and sister-in-law were not getting proper treatment to her.

33. In para 9, she has mentioned that for 5-6 months she had gone into NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:55490 7 CRA-4495-2025 depression as there was threat to viral her intimate videos.

However, in cross-examination, she has admitted several contradictions in her case diary statement (Ex.D-1) and supplementary statement (Ex.D-2).
Victim A vs Lakshya Keshwani on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69176187/
4 34.

In para 20, she admits that when they had spent about half an hour while having their dinner,
but when her husband and sister-in-law had not come, then she had asked Lakshya that since they have travelled for long and she is tired, she wanted to sleep.
She had asked Lakshya to go to his room, when he had gone back to his room and she had slept in her room.
If this is not mentioned in her case diary statements Ex.D-1 and Ex.D-2, then she cannot give any reasons for it.

35. In para 21, she admits that on 07.02.2021 at about 11:00 am, she had called her husband and asked that they have not reached the Jungle when her husband assured her to reach there by evening and asked her to go in the Jungle with Lakshya and undertake a Safari.
They returned back by 6:00 pm and if this is not mentioned in her statements Ex.D-1 and Ex.D-2, then she cannot explain it.
36. There are other contradictions in regard to food, lacing it with sedatives etc..
Reason given in the Court statements for delay in lodging FIR are contrary to the one mentioned in the FIR.
37. In para 32, victim admits that she had not reported the matter to the Manager of the Resort.
She admits that when in the morning she had travelled from the Resort to the tea shop, she had not informed anybody about the incident.
She further admits that she had travelled on the motorcycle of Lakshya and returned back on this motorcycle.

Motorcycle NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:55490 8 CRA-4495-2025 was being driven by Lakshya and she was a pillion rider.
38. In para 34, victim admits that on 07.02.2021 her brother had lodged a report at Police Station - Gorakhpur, Jabalpur against the co-accused Varun Dhakad and Vineeta Dhakad.
She admits that her statements were recorded at Gorakhpur Police Station and her address is of Jabalpur.
She admits that on the next day she and Lakshya had participated in Jungle Safari in a Bus and they were sitting adjacent to each other.
She admits that at Raisen also she had filed a case against Lakshya Keshwani in regard to violation of privacy.
She admits that Raisen case was brought to an end and subsequently she had withdrawn that case by visiting Office of Collector, Raisen.
She admits that she had made a complaint at Raisen in March, 2021 and thereafter lodged a report in regard to incident at Umariya.
39. In para 41, victim admits that she cannot give reason for delay in lodging of FIR.
She admits that Varun and Vineeta had not visited Bandhavgarh Resort and they did no wrong at Bandhavgarh.
She admits that she had given an application at one Stop Centre, Raisen to withdraw her case against Lakshya Keshwani.
She admits that she had entered into a compromise in writing.

40. In para 47, she admits that the case which was registered at Police Station Gorakhpur, Jabalpur,
registering Case Crime No.378/2021 was registered by her family members because she was admitted in hospital and her family members thought that her husband and nanad may have beaten her on account of demand of dowry.

This is also incorrect inasmuch as victim admits that she returned from Bandhavgarh on 8th February, 2021, thus there NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:55490 9 CRA-4495-2025 was no occasion to lodge a report on 07th February,
2021.

Victim A vs Lakshya Keshwani on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69176187/
5 41.
Ex.D-9 is her statements recorded on 08.04.2021.
She denied making statement in Ex.D-9 that she was beaten by her husband and nanad for want of a car.
She admits that after 07.02.2021 she did not visit her susral or her husband's house nor stayed there.

42. In para 63, she states that when she gained consciousness at Bhopal Hospital, she learnt that she was admitted at Jabalpur Hospital and since her husband was not getting her treatment, she was shifted to Bhopal.
43. In para 76, she admits that she had taken back her complaint at Raisen stating therein in writing that Lakshya Keshwani had not committed any incident with her.

44. In para 79, when victim was confronted with the photographs Article A and B to the effect that those photographs were not revealing any kind of opposition on her part but on the contrary reveals that she was voluntarily in embarrass with Lakshya, then she states that she has no knowledge as to when these photographs were taken.
She further states that later on she was informed that Lakshya Keshwani was threatening her to put these photographs on social media.
She admits seizure of photographs from her possession.

45. When these facts are taken into consideration along with evidence of Sanjay Yadav (PW-16),
Manager of the Resort, who admits that on Ex.P-28, register, name of the victim is not mentioned and on Ex.P13, Aadhar Card, there are no signatures of the victim. Dr. Abhishek Mishra (PW-11)
stated that Dr. Soniya Singh had taken consent of the victim and had recorded her NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:55490 10 CRA-4495-2025 history wherein she had stated that she was in friendship with the accused for last 10 months and in physical relationship for last 9 months and had proved the MLC report given by Dr. Soniya Singh (Ex.P-21) containing her signatures, and further admitting in cross-examination that in her history victim had never informed Dr. Soniya that she was given any sedative in the drink or her privacy was forcefully violated, we are of the opinion that overall conduct of the victim specially her conduct of lodging a report at Raisen and then withdrawing it and then subsequently filing another complaint in November, 2021 for a incident which took place in February, 2021 for which report was made in November, 2021 and prior to that a report was made in March, 2021 at Raisen, leaves no iota of doubt that delay in FIR to lodge report in November, 2021 is not made out.

46. When facts of the case along with the MLC are taken into consideration, then in the light of the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Chandrappa and others Vs. State of Karnataka, (2007) 4 SCC 415, we are of the opinion that firstly no two views are possible on evidence on record.

entities.text: Chandrappa and others Vs. State of Karnataka, (2007) 4 SCC 415
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: trial Court has rightly proceeded with the matter.

Though Appellate Court has power to review, reappreciate and reconsider the evidence upon which the order of acquittal is founded and Cr.P.C. do not put any limitation, restriction or condition on exercise of such power, but no material has been commended to us to take a view other than the one taken by the trial Court.
There is plethora of evidence to suggest that relationship between Lakshya Keshwani and appellant victim was consensual as is noted by Dr. Soniya Singh and proved by Dr. Abhishek Mishra (PW-11).

Matrimonial dispute NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:55490 11 CRA-4495-2025 between the victim and accused Nos.2 and 3 has been given an ugly turn and that too could not be substantiated including Victim A vs Lakshya Keshwani on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69176187/

6 demand of dowry or harassment related to demand of dowry and, therefore, when the holistic view of the evidence on record is taken into consideration, then in view of independent witnesses'
testimony, we are of the considered opinion that no view, other than the one taken by the trial Court, can be taken and there is no scope for showing indulgence in the matter.
47.
Therefore, I.A. No.10583/2025 for grant of leave to appeal under Section 378(4) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 fails and is hereby dismissed.
48. Resultantly, appeal filed under Section 41 of the Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 against the judgment of acquittal dated 20.12.2024 passed in S.T. No.33/2022 is also dismissed.
